slot.brief: Structure of an alkene (di-substituted, in figure) undergoes ozonolysis with Zn/H2O; identify the carbonyl fragments formed.

stem: The alkene shown in the figure is treated with $\text{O}_3$, followed by $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Which carbonyl products are formed?

verdicts.working: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C into two aldehydes. The left side gives 2-methylpropanal; the right side gives 2-methylbutanal.

working:
$(CH_3)_2CHCH=CHCH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3 \xrightarrow{\text{O}_3,\ \text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}} (CH_3)_2CHCHO + CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CHO$

Independent check: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C into two aldehydes. The left side gives 2-methylpropanal; the right side gives 2-methylbutanal.
solution:
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond, converting each alkene carbon bearing a hydrogen into an aldehyde carbonyl.
$$ (CH_3)_2CHCH=CHCH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3 \\xrightarrow{O_3,\ Zn/H_2O} (CH_3)_2CHCHO + CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CHO $$
The products are 2-methylpropanal and 2-methylbutanal.

figure.description: Draw a horizontal C=C. The left alkene carbon is bonded to H and CH(CH3)2; the right alkene carbon is bonded to H and CH(CH3)CH2CH3. Show the branches explicitly. Do not indicate E/Z stereochemistry.

draft.distractor_notes:
B assigns a ketone to a double-bond carbon that bears hydrogen.
C ignores the methyl branches when identifying the fragments.
D misallocates the carbon atoms between the two fragments.
